issues: The location is specified as Laban’s house, but the verse only says Nephi came near the house; it does not establish that Laban was inside it. Depicting the encounter as inside the house would be unsupported.

The location is specified as Laban’s house, but the verse only says Nephi came near the house; it does not establish that Laban was inside it. Depicting the encounter as inside the house would be unsupported.
Lettering must be an exact source quotation
The servant is incorrectly labeled “Laman’s servant”; the source identifies him as Laban’s servant.
Lettering must be an exact source quotation
“Return to Jerusalem” in the summary overstates the verse’s “go up again” (which is a renewed attempt); otherwise the scene’s facts and quotations are supported.
Nephi is explicitly said to creep into the city and go toward Laban’s house; “moves cautiously” is a reasonable inference, but “through the city” may imply more than the text specifies.
Lettering must be an exact source quotation

The summary says Nephi sees the servant and commands him to enter the treasury; the verse says Nephi sees him while going toward the treasury and commands him to go with Nephi into it. The quoted fragment is verbatim but begins mid-sentence.

The summary’s “the church” wording accurately reports the servant’s mistaken supposition, but could be misconstrued as establishing a church or group present in the scene; the scene notes correctly prohibit depicting such a group.

The summary says the brothers suppose Nephi is Laban, who has slain Nephi; this is their mistaken belief, not an event occurring in this scene. The scene notes appropriately prohibit showing the imagined killing.
Narration is not an exact contiguous quotation: the source says “not knowing beforehand the things which I should do,” not “not knowing beforehand what I should do.”
Dialogue for verse 1 Nephi 4:13 is not verbatim: it omits “Behold the Lord slayeth the wicked to bring forth his righteous purposes.”

Lettering must be an exact source quotation: 'I knew that the law was engraven upon the plates of brass.' is not verbatim in 1 Nephi 4:16, which reads 'And I also knew that the law was engraven upon the plates of brass.'
“Servant holds or carries the treasury keys” is a reasonable inference; the text only says he had them.
The identity of “Nephi’s brothers” is not explicitly named in verses 30–31; depicting them without identifying details is safest.
Summary says the brothers are urged to be faithful, but omits the quoted appeal to go up again; this is a minor incompleteness.
Nephi addresses his brethren; only scene 2 explicitly identifies Laman, Lemuel, and Sam among them, so identifying this group as those named brothers here is contextual inference.

Summary changes the chronology: verse 5 places the brothers hiding outside the walls before Nephi enters the city, but says they remain hidden as Nephi moves through the city toward Laban’s house; verse 6 reports his being led by the Spirit, not a spoken statement.
The inference that Nephi approaches Laban is reasonable from “when I came to him,” but the exact action is not otherwise specified.
The verse reports Nephi’s inward thoughts and shrinking; depicting him visibly hesitating with the sword near Laban is a reasonable but unspecified visual interpretation.

The quoted line attributed to the Spirit from verse 13 is not verbatim: the source begins “Behold the Lord slayeth the wicked to bring forth his righteous purposes.” The supplied dialogue changes this into a different sentence.
The verse 14 excerpt is a contiguous exact quotation but begins mid-sentence; as narration it may misleadingly present only a fragment of the remembered conditional promise.
“Holds or carries the treasury keys” is not established; the verse says the servant had the keys, without specifying how they are held.

The verse 24 dialogue excerpt is exact, but the verse 25 excerpt “that he should follow me” is narration rendered as a fragment of Nephi’s speech; the source says Nephi bade him to follow, without supplying those words as direct dialogue.
The selected verse 32 dialogue fragment is exact but omits the verse’s conditional and oath context, which could make the offer sound unconditional.
The summary says Nephi "says" he is led by the Spirit, but verse 4:6 is narration, not spoken dialogue.
The narration excerpt "they shall prosper in the land of promise." omits the source verse's initial capital as supplied, violating the exact-quotation requirement.

The quote "that he should go with me into the treasury." is an exact contiguous excerpt, but the leading lower-case 'that' has no quoted subject/context, so attribution to Nephi's command may be unclear.
The quote "that he should follow me." is narration reporting Nephi's instruction, not Nephi's verbatim spoken words; the source does not supply the exact words Nephi said.
The quoted fragments from verses 4:32–34 are narration reporting Nephi's speech, not verbatim dialogue spoken by Nephi; the source does not provide these phrases as his exact words.

The servant supposes Nephi means the brethren of the church, but the text does not say the servant believes Nephi is Laban at this point; that mistaken identity is already stated in verse 21, however, so the fact itself is supported.
